points.quote: Before using any AI to support an assessment, you should always check and follow your assessment brief and your tutor’s guidance on use of AI.
points.gist: Before using AI for an assessment, check and follow your assessment brief and your tutor's guidance.

points.quote: You are unable to use AI for the final output of the assessment due to the assessment design. For example, a closed book exam where you are required to demonstrate within controlled conditions that you have core knowledge or a skill in a particular area.
points.gist: In Category 1 you cannot use AI for the final output because of the assessment design, for example a closed book exam.

points.quote: You may make use of AI in your assessment in an assistive role, but you must acknowledge this appropriately.
points.anchor: Category 2: AI can be used in an assistive role
points.gist: In Category 2 you may use AI in an assistive role but must acknowledge it appropriately.

points.quote: Using AI is part of the assessment and will be expected. You must still acknowledge where and how you have used AI.
points.anchor: Category 3: AI is an integral part of assessment
points.gist: In Category 3 AI use is expected as part of the assessment, but you must still acknowledge where and how you used it.

points.quote: If you have used AI in a piece of assessed work at UON, you must make it clear where and how you have used AI output, not doing so can be seen as Academic Misconduct.
points.anchor: Step 2: When do I need to acknowledge using AI?
points.gist: If you used AI in assessed work you must make clear where and how; failing to do so can be seen as academic misconduct.

points.quote: Some uses of AI are seen as ‘permitted use’ and do not normally require an acknowledgement in your work. These include:
points.gist: Some permitted uses do not normally require acknowledgement.
Checking spelling, punctuation and grammar is a permitted use not normally needing acknowledgement.

points.quote: Generating text, images or any other content to add to your assessment.
points.gist: Generating text, images or other content to add to your assessment is a higher-risk use requiring acknowledgement.

points.quote: If your use of AI is not listed above, you should check first with your tutor to see if your use of AI is allowed in your assessment.
points.anchor: Step 2: When do I need to acknowledge using AI?
points.gist: If your AI use is not listed, check first with your tutor whether it is allowed.

points.quote: Use AI outputs that you do not understand or cannot explain.
points.anchor: You must not use AI to:
points.gist: Do not use AI outputs that you do not understand or cannot explain.

points.quote: A simple guideline: If you cannot explain, defend, or reproduce the work yourself, you should not submit it.
points.anchor: You must not use AI to:
points.gist: If you cannot explain, defend or reproduce the work yourself, you should not submit it.

points.quote: This should include the name of the AI software that you used and a clear description of where and how the output was used in your work.
points.anchor: Step 3: How do I acknowledge using AI?
points.gist: An acknowledgement should include the name of the AI software and a clear description of where and how the output was used.

points.quote: Acknowledgements should be included as appendices in your assessment.
points.anchor: Step 3: How do I acknowledge using AI?
points.gist: Acknowledgements should be included as appendices in your assessment.

points.quote: The GenAI Acknowledgement Generator is a tool designed to help you write an acknowledgement when you have used GenAI in a piece of assessment work.
points.anchor: Step 3: How do I acknowledge using AI?
points.gist: The GenAI Acknowledgement Generator helps you write an acknowledgement when you have used GenAI in assessment work.

points.quote: The following should not be submitted to an AI tool: confidential data; data belonging to other people or organisations, i.e. the intellectual property of other people or third-party copyrighted material, unless permission has been granted or is licensed; your own personal data, unless you are prepared for it to surface in AI output.
points.gist: Do not submit confidential data, others' data or third-party copyrighted material without permission, or your own personal data unless prepared for it to surface.

points.quote: UON advises its university community to use AI tools purposefully and only when they add value to your learning or work.
points.gist: The university advises using AI tools purposefully and only when they add value to your learning or work.

points.quote: You are advised to complete the University of Northampton Plagiarism Avoidance Course, usually known as UNPAC to learn more about academic integrity.
points.gist: You are advised to complete the Plagiarism Avoidance Course, UNPAC, to learn more about academic integrity.
